item.title: Briefing — Friday, November 27
item.description: Why Pursuing Absolute U.S. AI Dominance Over China Increases Catastrophic Risk; Synthetic protein system restores chromosome stability in aging eggs, showing potential for IVF; Montana’s expanded ‘right to try’ law threatens clinical trial integrity and patient finances; Vyriad lands Big Pharma partnerships for in vivo CAR-T cell delivery platforms; Pakistani architect Kamil Khan Mumtaz abandoned modernism to revive centuries-old traditional craftsmanship.

item.title: Briefing — Thursday, November 26
item.description: Medicare’s 2027 physician payment cuts threaten the viability of small specialist practices; ARM CEO Tim Hunt details industry pushback against FDA's shifting gene therapy regulatory stance; ProPublica Analysis Reveals Doubling of Ectopic Pregnancy Deaths in States with Abortion Bans; Political Instability and Far-Right Gains Threaten European Union Cohesion and Strategic Autonomy; San Diego-based Iambic Therapeutics reports promising preclinical data for AI-designed oncology candidates

item.title: Briefing — Wednesday, November 25
item.description: U.S.-China Biotech Decoupling Risks Stifling Innovation Rather Than Protecting National Interests; Chilling Effect of Immigration Policy Drives Significant Decline in International Biomedical Graduate Enrollment; Election outcomes reflect economic dissatisfaction rather than a global anti-authoritarian democratic revival; Pentagon Considers Massive $15 Billion Loan to AI Defense Startup Linked to Trump Jr.; AI industry leaders clash over the ethics of surrendering human decision-making to superintelligence
